title: Strict transforms under a composition of blow-ups
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, and put $b_0:S_1=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(S)\to S$ [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Let $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_{S_1}$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, and put $b_1:S_2=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}(S_1)\to S_1$. Let $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal equipped with an isomorphism $S_2\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}(S)$ over $S$ identifying $b_0b_1$ with the blow-up map. Assume the equality of subsets $V(\mathcal K)=V(\mathcal I)\cup b_0(V(\mathcal J))$. For every scheme morphism $X\to S$, let $X_1$ be its strict transform along $b_0$, and let $X_2$ be the strict transform of $X_1\to S_1$ along $b_1$ [def-nagata-strict-transform]. Under the specified isomorphism and the associative identification of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product], $X_2$ is canonically isomorphic to the strict transform of $X\to S$ along $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}(S)\to S$, compatibly with the closed inclusions into $X\times_S S_2$ and the projections to $X$ and $S_2$.

source.place: Tag 080I, lemma-strict-transform-composition-blowups, clause (2) (scheme strict transforms). The support equality of the three centers is part of its hypotheses.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$ and denote by $\mathcal F'$ and $\mathcal F''$ its successive strict transforms along $b_0$ and $b_1$, while $\mathcal G$ denotes its strict transform along the specified composite blow-up $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}(S)\to S$. Let $p:X\times_S S_1\to X$ and $q:X\times_S S_2\to X\times_S S_1$ be the base-change projections. By [def-trf-module-strict-transform], each module strict transform here is the quotient by the local sections vanishing off the inverse image of the exceptional subscheme, with the centre ideal retained. Applying [lem-trf-strict-transform-sheaf-kernel] first to $b_0$ and $\mathcal F$, and then to $b_1$, the morphism $X\times_SS_1\to S_1$ and $\mathcal F'$ (which is quasi-coherent by the first application), gives canonical surjections $p^*\mathcal F\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F'$ and $q^*\mathcal F'\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F''$, whose kernels are supported over the inverse images of $V(\mathcal I)$ and $V(\mathcal J)$ respectively. Right exactness of pullback combines them into a surjection $(p\circ q)^*\mathcal F\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F''$; its kernel is supported on the union of those two inverse images.

source.place: Tag 080I, proof of lemma-strict-transform-composition-blowups, opening construction through the paragraph identifying the support of the kernel.

proof.text: The same pullback $(p\circ q)^*\mathcal F$ has the canonical surjection to $\mathcal G$. Since $V(\mathcal K)=V(\mathcal I)\cup b_0(V(\mathcal J))$, the support of the kernel of the first surjection is contained in the inverse image of $V(\mathcal K)$ in $X\times_S S_2$. The kernel description in [lem-trf-strict-transform-sheaf-kernel] for the composite blow-up therefore makes this surjection factor canonically as $(p\circ q)^*\mathcal F\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F''\longrightarrow\mathcal G$.

source.place: Tag 080I, proof of lemma-strict-transform-composition-blowups, paragraph beginning 'By construction of \mathcal{G} we see that we obtain a factorization'.

proof.text: By [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center], the total transform $E=b_0^{-1}V(\mathcal I)$ on $S_1$ is an effective Cartier divisor. The sheaf $\mathcal F'$ has no nonzero local sections supported over the inverse image of $V(\mathcal I)$ by [lem-trf-strict-transform-sheaf-kernel]. Apply [lem-trf-strict-transform-different-centers] on the base $S_1$, with center $V(\mathcal J)$, Cartier divisor $E$, and the quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal F'$ on $X\times_SS_1$; the product ideal $\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal I\mathcal O_{S_1}$ is again of finite type, being locally generated by the products of finitely many generators of $\mathcal J$ with one local generator of $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{S_1}$. The existing comparison [lemma-nagata-blowup-invertible-factor] identifies the blow-up of $S_1$ in the product center $V(\mathcal J)\cdot E$ with the blow-up in $V(\mathcal J)$, so the different-centers lemma identifies $\mathcal F''$ with the strict transform obtained by blowing up that product center. View $b_0$ as the $U$-admissible blow-up for $U=S\setminus V(\mathcal I)$. By [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open], $b_0$ is an isomorphism over $U$; consequently the inverse image of $b_0(V(\mathcal J))$ in $S_2$ is the union of the inverse image of $V(\mathcal I)$ and the inverse image of $V(\mathcal J)$. After pullback to $X\times_S S_2$, the inverse image of the product center is therefore exactly that same union, hence is the inverse image of $V(\mathcal K)$ by the assumed support equality.

source.place: Tag 080I proof, final paragraph, applying Tag 080H (lemma-strict-transform-different-centers) to the first strict transform and the effective Cartier total transform.

proof.text: The strict transform for the product center has no nonzero local sections supported on its center by [lem-trf-strict-transform-sheaf-kernel]. Thus the kernel of the induced map $\mathcal F''\to\mathcal G$ in the factorization of Step 2, which is supported on the inverse image of $V(\mathcal K)$ because both sheaves agree away from that inverse image, is zero. The factorization is therefore an isomorphism. To pass from modules to schemes, let $i_1:X_1\hookrightarrow X\times_S S_1$ and $i_2:X_2\hookrightarrow X_1\times_{S_1}S_2$ be the closed immersions defining the successive scheme strict transforms. The $\mathcal O_X$ clause of [lem-trf-strict-transform-sheaf-kernel] identifies the first module strict transform with $i_{1,*}\mathcal O_{X_1}$. Pullback along the base-changed closed immersion commutes with this pushforward by the defining affine sheaf/module formula, and [lem-trf-strict-transform-affine-pushforward] applied to the affine map $i_1$ identifies the second module strict transform with $i_{2,*}\mathcal O_{X_2}$. The same kernel clause identifies $\mathcal G$ with the structure sheaf of the composite scheme strict transform. Hence the module isomorphism is induced by an isomorphism of the two closed subschemes in the common ambient fibre product; equivalently, they are the same smallest closed subscheme through which the preserved open factors by [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-closure-characterization].

source.place: Tag 080I proof of lemma-strict-transform-composition-blowups, conclusion after the support argument.

proof.text: All identifications above are induced by the canonical pullback maps, the specified isomorphism $S_2\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}(S)$, and the universal property of the fibre products. Consequently the isomorphism is compatible with the closed inclusions into $X\times_S S_2$ and with the projections to $X$ and $S_2$, under the associative fibre-product identification in [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 080I, statement and proof: compatibility with the common ambient fibre product and the projections.

proof_origin.place: Tag 080I, lemma-strict-transform-composition-blowups, scheme clause (2), proof using clause (1) and Tag 080H.

tool_uses.why: The route needs the standard fact that the first blow-up makes the center ideal an effective Cartier divisor; the trace-formula unit has no replacement for this blow-up tool.

The final passage from the structure-sheaf comparison to equality of scheme strict transforms uses the scheme-theoretic closure characterization, which is a generic strict-transform tool from the Nagata unit.

lean.statement: theorem strictTransform_comp_blowup (S X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ S) (I : S.IdealSheafData) (hI : I.ofFiniteType) (J : I.blowup.IdealSheafData) (hJ : J.ofFiniteType) (K : S.IdealSheafData) (hK : K.ofFiniteType) (e : J.blowup ≅ K.blowup) (he : J.blowupMap ≫ I.blowupMap = e.hom ≫ K.blowupMap) (hV : (K.support : Set S) = (I.support : Set S) ∪ I.blowupMap '' (J.support : Set I.blowup)) : ∃ φ : secondStrictTransform I J f ≅ K.strictTransform f, φ.hom ≫ K.strictTransformι f ≫ pullback.fst f K.blowupMap = secondStrictTransformι I J f ≫ pullback.fst (firstStrictTransformToSource I f) J.blowupMap ≫ AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransformι f I.blowupMap I.support.compl ≫ pullback.fst f I.blowupMap ∧ φ.hom ≫ K.strictTransformι f ≫ pullback.snd f K.blowupMap ≫ e.inv = secondStrictTransformι I J f ≫ pullback.snd (firstStrictTransformToSource I f) J.blowupMap
